label: Christopher K. Mellon
narrative: Mellon is the strategist of the current cycle. He is Board Chair of the Disclosure Foundation, and the FY2026 NDAA's three UAP provisions - the NORAD/NORTHCOM intercept briefing requirement, the accounting for UAP security classification guides, and the streamlining of agency data-sharing with AARO - reflect recommendations from him and the Foundation. That is legislative drafting influence, not commentary, and the intercept provision in particular is the sharpest instrument in the current statutory record because it presumes and demands an operational history rather than a sighting inventory. On 20 February 2026, hours after the President's post, his assessment was 'This might be a consequential moment, but the impact will depend on the follow-through... The public's trust has been eroded and must be restored.' On 14 May 2026, six days after the first tranche, he delivered the judgement that has framed everything since: 'Data alone is not disclosure. Releasing raw files without context may confuse more than clarify.' Mellon is the figure who most clearly held both positions at once through 2026 - that the release programme is real and that it is not disclosure - and both of his 2026 statements have proved load-bearing on the record.
